newsitem.title: USA: Danaher says seeks friendly Exide deal, may up bid.
newsitem.headline: Danaher says seeks friendly Exide deal, may up bid.

text.p: Danaher Corp said in a letter to its takeover target Exide Electronics Group Inc that it would consider raising its $20 per share unsolicited bid if Exide agreed to reveal confidential company information.

In the July 9 letter to Exide chief executive James Risher from Danaher chief executive George Sherman, it also was revealed that Exide refused a $22 per share offer from Danaher that would have been subject to confidential due diligence and negotiations.
Sherman also said a $20 per share bid for Exide was first made in a June 11 letter to Exide.
Risher's office did not immediately return telephone calls seeking comment.

"We are particularly disappointed that the (Exide) board did not wish to pursue our offer of $22 per share subject to confidential due diligence and negotiations. While we continue to strongly prefer a negotiated transaction, in light of the responses from your board of directors, we feel compelled to pursue this matter more expeditiously," the letter states.

Early Wednesday, Danaher announced the commencement of a cash tender offer for Exide at $20 per share, a bid based only on public information on Exide, and filed a lawsuit against Exide to force the company into a deal.

Danaher, a Washington, D.C.-based maker of tools, process and environmental controls and transportation products, also called for a special meeting of Exide shareholders to elect Danaher's slate of directors "and otherwise expedite the acquisition."
Exide is headquartered in Raleigh, N.C.. The company makes uninterruptable power supply systems and power manangement software.
